summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with advanced multiple sclerosis and a chronic indwelling Foley catheter, was admitted with weakness and hypotension due to septic shock from a Proteus mirabilis urinary tract infection and bacteremia. He presented with a distended bladder and hydronephrosis due to catheter malposition, which was corrected in the emergency department. He required brief vasopressor support and was treated with intravenous antibiotics, transitioning from piperacillin-tazobactam to ceftriaxone after culture results. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic therapy. Acute kidney injury improved with supportive care. Complications included a penile erosion from long-term catheter use and recurrent ostomy prolapse, both addressed with surgical and urological follow-up plans. He stabilized over eight days and was discharged home with services for continued IV antibiotics and specialist appointments.
